list_of_rare_earth_compounds.compound_name: Praseodymium–lithium cyclooctatetraenyl chloride cluster, toluene disolvate
list_of_rare_earth_compounds.formula: C92 H160 Cl8 Li2 O2 Pr6 Si12·2(C7 H8)

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: The discrete Pr6Li2 cluster is built around a cube of eight chloride atoms. Two Pr(COT′′) half-sandwich units, two Pr2(COT′′)2 sandwich units, and two Li(THF) units cap its faces. The article also describes a Pr4Li2 octahedral arrangement within the cluster core, whose eight faces are capped by chloride atoms. COT′′ is 1,4-bis(trimethylsilyl)cyclooctatetraenyl; the crystallized material contains two toluene molecules per formula unit.

synthesis.procedure: Li2(COT′′) was generated in situ by double deprotonation of 1,4-bis(trimethylsilyl)-1,3,5-cyclooctatriene with 2 equivalents of n-butyllithium in THF, then reacted with anhydrous PrCl3 in THF. The room-temperature reaction took approximately two weeks to approach completion, followed by one hour of heating at reflux. Insoluble material was removed by careful filtration.
synthesis.temperature: Room temperature, then THF reflux; slow cooling for crystallization
synthesis.time: Approximately 2 weeks at room temperature, then 1 hour at reflux
synthesis.vessel_or_method: In situ ligand preparation followed by solution reaction
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Insoluble PrCl3 and LiCl were removed by careful filtration. The product was recrystallized from toluene; slow cooling gave orange-yellow, needle-like X-ray-quality crystals containing two toluene molecules per formula unit.

title: A Unique Organolanthanide Cluster Containing Bulky Cyclooctatetraenyl Ligands
